Summary
: This is the English translation of the Ganita-sara-sangraha by Mahavira Acharya—an ancient Sanskrit text dealing with mathematics and mathematical problems from the 9th century. The Ganitasarasangraha includes significant mathematical concepts, like the decimal notation system and operations involving zero, highlighting the embedded rich mathematical culture among Indian scholars.
The Ganita-sara-samgraha also investigates the connections and influences between different schools of mathematics in India and abroad. Despite Greek influences on geometry seen in ancient Indian mathematics, Mahavira's work appears distinctively independent in its algebraic treatment.
